issues.legal_issue: A buyer remains ready and willing to perform an agreement to sell when the seller has not fulfilled agreed prerequisites to payment and the buyer deposits the balance when directed by the court.
material_facts: The seller admitted that the land was to be measured, the consideration determined, and the original sale deed delivered before completion.
The land was not measured, and the seller did not provide the buyer with the original title deed or final land-ceiling documents.
The buyer repeatedly sought those documents and completion of the agreed steps.
The buyer deposited the balance consideration within the extended time allowed by the trial court.
The trial court and the High Court found that the seller had failed to perform her part of the agreement and that the buyer was ready and willing to perform.
issues.conclusion: The buyer's readiness and willingness were established, and the decree for specific performance was upheld. The buyer's failure to demonstrate that he held the balance consideration at an earlier point, including the fact that he later deposited money received from a property sale, did not alter that result.
issues.legal_principle: Readiness and willingness must be assessed in light of the parties' agreed obligations and their conduct. Where the seller has not fulfilled agreed prerequisites to completion, the buyer is not required to pay the balance before those prerequisites are met. A deposit made when the court directs it supports the buyer's bona fides; the later source of the deposited funds does not, by itself, establish that the buyer was previously unable to pay. The judgment does not apply a statutory provision or earlier case as controlling on this issue; it distinguishes the authorities cited by the seller in light of the concurrent factual findings.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and seller_admitted_completion_prerequisites and seller_failed_completion_prerequisites and buyer_deposited_balance_when_directed

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The buyer brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.seller_admitted_completion_prerequisites: The seller admitted that specified steps, including measuring the land and delivering title documents, were to be completed before the sale was finalized.
predicates.seller_failed_completion_prerequisites: The seller did not complete the agreed steps before the buyer was required to pay the balance and complete the purchase.
predicates.buyer_deposited_balance_when_directed: The buyer deposited the balance consideration when the court directed the deposit and within the time allowed.

issues.definition: When a buyer seeks specific performance, the seller admitted agreed completion prerequisites, the seller failed to complete them, and the buyer deposited the balance when directed, the specific-performance decree is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A seller appealing a decree for specific performance cannot obtain relief on a hardship ground that was not pleaded in the defence.
material_facts: The seller argued on appeal that granting specific performance after many years would cause undue hardship.
The seller had not pleaded hardship in the written statement.
issues.conclusion: The hardship argument could not be entertained on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A hardship plea against specific performance cannot be raised for the first time on appeal when it was not pleaded in the written statement. The Court relied on A. Maria Angelena v. A.G. Balkis Bee, AIR 2002 SC 2385, which likewise rejected a hardship plea first raised at the appellate stage.

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The seller appealed a decree granting specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.hardship_not_pleaded_in_defence: The seller did not plead in the defence that granting specific performance would cause hardship.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a decree for specific performance, a seller who did not plead hardship in the defence cannot have that hardship plea entertained.
